passage:
The school required black shoes, but Leo's family could not buy a new pair right away. His old shoes were dark blue.
Leo worried that teachers would notice. One morning, the discipline teacher stopped him at the gate. Leo looked down, ready to be scolded.
The teacher asked quietly if everything was all right. Leo explained. The teacher nodded and gave him a note that allowed him to wear the shoes for two weeks.
Later, the school started a shoe exchange box. Students could leave clean shoes they no longer wore.
Rules were still important, but the school learned that rules should leave room for understanding people's real lives.
